unrecordedQuestions: Locked in: a shared read-only renderer backs both Preview (renders the live in-progress draft) and View (renders a locked/published snapshot); Continue to builder opens the builder pre-populated with the values just pulled. (For the record, resolved from existing code, no need to answer: insights are already autosaved on every keystroke — `editKpi` persists the whole draft to disk on each change, same as values — so there's no separate save/blur step to design. Target and delta-vs-last-MBR aren't literally "pulled" over the network; target comes from config and delta is computed from the value plus the last published snapshot, so they're just rendered alongside the value once it lands.) Next real decision: the mockup shows the builder toolbar with its own dark/light theme toggle, but I checked and this app has NO existing global theme system at all today — there's nothing app-wide for the builder to "follow" instead. Building one would be a real scope expansion beyond an MBR builder redesign. Should I keep the mockup's own local toggle scoped to just this view (as drawn), or do you want this mission to also introduce app-wide theming? (offered choices: Keep the mockup's own toggle, scoped to just this view; Introduce app-wide theming as part of this mission) (its recommendation: Keep the mockup's own toggle, scoped to just this view — there's no app-wide theme system to hook into today, and building one is a separate concern from an MBR builder redesign)

So "follow global" needs a source to follow. Should this mission add a minimal global toggle control somewhere in the app's main chrome (outside the builder) that the builder then reads, or should the builder just follow the OS/browser's `prefers-color-scheme` with no manual toggle control anywhere at all?
